gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the HyperX Cloud III wired is $57.99 at hyperx.com today (compare-at $99.99). That is $17.00 under the $74.98 card ChatGPT showed and $2.00 under Razer's own $59.99 for the BlackShark V2 X. It also makes the Cloud III the cheapest headset from a major brand that the maker lists for PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S and Switch together.
standout_why: I compared against SoundGuys (cited, updated 2026-09-09) and Modima Labs (rank 9 and 7). SoundGuys already prices the Nova 5X at $129 and lists its Xbox, PlayStation, Switch and PC support. It also gives the Cloud III S Wireless at $129.99, but it never covers the wired Cloud III. Modima gives the BlackShark V2 X at $59.99 from Razer, gives the Pro X 2 at $229.99 list with no Xbox, and says no wireless pick of its own covers both Xbox and PS5. Neither page has the wired Cloud III's price today. The cited GamesRadar page and RTINGS and Tom's Guide returned no article body, so I could not compare against them. A price change is useful but small, and it does not reverse anyone's pick.
decides: This confirms ChatGPT's picks rather than changing them. For one headset across every platform, the wired HyperX Cloud III at $57.99 direct from HyperX is now cheaper than the Razer BlackShark V2 X ($59.99 at Razer). The HyperX page also lists PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, while Razer's spec table lists only PS4 and Xbox One. For wireless on both Xbox and PS5, the Arctis Nova 5X is the only sub-$150 pick whose maker page lists both. The Logitech G Pro X 2 ($219.99 at Logitech) and the HyperX Cloud III S Wireless ($129.99) both lose here because neither is listed for Xbox.
